body:
VERIFIED ORIGIN BOUNDARY — recommendation: keep controller, presenter view, audience/projector view, and shared worker/service worker under ONE exact origin (same scheme+host+port), differentiated by paths/routes. Put only server-only APIs/admin/internal services on separate origins/subdomains.

Why this materially matters:
1) `app.example.com` and `present.example.com` are different origins because origin is scheme/host/port; subdomains do not qualify as same-origin. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Same-origin_policy
2) A cross-origin `window.opener` is only a restricted WindowProxy. You cannot read variables/functions/DOM; only a limited allowlist such as `postMessage`, `close`, `focus`, `blur`, `closed`, and limited navigation remains. All other property access throws SecurityError. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/opener
3) Cross-origin windows can synchronize with `window.postMessage`, but every send must use an exact `targetOrigin`, and every receiver must validate `event.origin` (and ideally `event.source`). This is viable but adds a security-critical protocol and loses direct shared state/DOM access. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage
4) `BroadcastChannel` works only among same-origin contexts in the same storage partition. Separate subdomains cannot share a channel. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Broadcast_Channel_API
5) Service workers are origin-bound: registration rejects unless `scriptURL` and scope are same-origin with the registering page. Separate UI subdomains therefore require independent registrations/caches/update lifecycles. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ServiceWorkerContainer/register
6) COOP can sever opener even for otherwise expected relationships. `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` isolates browsing context groups and prevents a cross-origin opener reference; if cross-origin UI is unavoidable, ensure header strategy does not accidentally null/sever the channel, or use an explicit server relay/WebSocket. MDN: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy
7) `document.domain` relaxation is deprecated and has limitations; do not use it as an architecture escape hatch. Same-origin policy source above.

Architecture boundary: SAME ORIGIN `/control`, `/presenter`, `/stage`, `/assets`, `/sw.js`; use BroadcastChannel as the resilient fan-out bus and optionally retain direct Window refs only for lifecycle/focus/close. SEPARATE ORIGIN only for API calls that do not need browser-window coordination (e.g. `api.example.com`), with CORS/auth or reverse-proxy it behind `/api`. If sensitive admin is hosted separately, communicate server-side rather than joining the presentation window mesh. This preserves Window Management placement (which itself can open any URL) while avoiding avoidable opener/channel/SW fragmentation.
summary: Extended mode should keep all UI windows same-origin
